title: Build a website
blurb: One agent writes code with fs, mounts a Workspace only to install, build and serve, publishes to main, then sees publish overwrite main and merges to keep both.

root.say: I'll fork a Branch for this task, and a second one, late, to show what publish does later.

bash.description: Fork feature-home and late from main

root.note: A fork is metadata only: nothing is copied. Both Branches start from main's first Layer.

root.say: The headline and an About page are plain file changes, so fs is enough: no Sandbox needed.

bash.description: Write the headline and About page

root.note: Each fs write is a Commit on feature-home.

root.say: Installing and building needs a shell, so now I mount feature-home in a Sandbox.
root.note: The build fails lint on the unescaped apostrophe in the About page.

root.say: The lint error is the apostrophe. I'll fix it inside the Workspace and build again.

bash.description: Fix the apostrophe; build and test

root.say: Serving the site in the background, then trying to unmount while it runs.

bash.description: Serve the site; try to unmount

root.note: Unmount is refused while a process runs in the Workspace.

root.say: Stopping the server first, then committing the fix with the build output.

bash.description: Stop the server; commit and clean up

root.say: feature-home is built and verified. Publishing it to main.
root.note: Publish adds a Layer to main; publishing the same Commit again is UpToDate.

root.say: late was forked before that publish. Watch what publishing it does to main.

bash.description: Write on late and publish it

root.note: Publish overwrites: main now has exactly late's files, so the About page left main. Its Layer stays in history.

root.say: To keep both, merge before publishing.
root.note: Merge never changes its inputs: both is a new Branch holding feature-home's and late's work.

root.reply: main has the headline, the About page and late's page. Publish replaces main with a Branch, so merge first when main has moved.
